process_type: Atomic Layer Deposition (ALD) with UV radiation
summary: Aluminum oxide thin films were deposited using atomic layer deposition (ALD) with trimethylaluminum (TMA) and water under UV radiation. The films were prepared at two different temperatures, 260°C and 370°C. The study investigated the effects of UV radiation on the structural and electrical properties of the films, including changes in the O/Al atomic ratio, valence band structure, and leakage current density. The results showed that UV radiation reduced carbon contamination and improved the insulating properties of the films.
evidence: Aluminum oxide thin films were deposited by atomic layer deposition using trimethylaluminum and water under UV radiation. Films were prepared at two different deposition temperatures of 260 and 370°C. The films deposited at 370°C had a higher O/Al atomic ratio than those deposited at 260°C. The upper valence band spectrum, observed by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, of the aluminum oxide thin film deposited under UV radiation during water purge was different from that of a nonradiated thin film, indicating a structural change by the UV radiation.
